key_insight: Weak magnetic fields can strengthen, weaken or reverse hydrodynamic coupling between ferrofluid rotors, with source position determining the response.
engineering_relevance: Magnetic placement and heating offer contactless control of fluid-mediated rotor motion, potentially enabling tunable microscale transmissions.
method: Coupled MHD–FHD model with full Kelvin force and temperature-dependent Langevin magnetisation.
Taylor–Hood finite elements solve steady flow and the torque-free passive rotor’s gear ratio.
Swept magnetic-source arrangements, rotor gaps, Reynolds numbers and heating levels.
evidence_signal: About 17,000 steady states covered 34 source arrangements; zero-field results agreed within 1–8% with published planar simulations, while 2 mT fields altered coupling in nine cases out of ten.
watch_item: Results are steady numerical predictions for a specific ferrofluid and confined geometry; transient behavior and experimental transfer require validation.
paper_title: Magnetic control of hydrodynamic spin coupling between rotors: Ferrohydrodynamic effects in the two-rotor problem
